The bill sets faster agency review timelines, shortens the window to sue from years to 150 days, makes it harder for courts to block projects under the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act, and Endangered Species Act (allowing construction even if a federal environmental review is ruled deficient), narrows state and Tribes' authority to deny projects over water pollution, gives the government greater power to approve transmission when states delay them, softens an initial provision that would have eliminated utilities' right of first refusal for grid upgrades, and includes "permit certainty" provisions banning administrations from vacating issued permits except in emergencies or under new laws. A Rhodium Group forecast attributes a 1% to 18% reduction in power sector emissions by 2040 (depending on clean energy's price competitiveness with gas) and $50 to $78 lower average annual household electricity bills, though it excludes behind-the-meter data center gas plants; these are forecasts, not established outcomes. Trump endorsed the bill via Truth Social, and a White House ratepayer protection pledge would effectively double charges for data centers' new transmission lines and existing grid use, with implementation left to FERC.
items.title: Senate passes bipartisan permitting reform bill in 62-33 vote

items.summary: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez acknowledged his government had made "mistakes" but insisted it has always governed in the right direction, opening Thursday's campaign-deciding televised debate against conservative rival Alberto Núñez Feijóo. The two clashed over the economy, housing, immigration, corruption and foreign policy amid a November 29 election that could bring far-right Vox into government if no majority forms. Sánchez cited economic growth and employment figures to argue Spain is in better shape than when he took power in 2018; Feijóo rejected this, accusing the government of crushing the middle class while families struggle with soaring prices and a housing crisis. Polls show Socialists trailing PP, which is predicted to win most seats without a majority, leaving Vox as decisive third force after it governed regionally with PP in 2023; Sánchez's weakened left-wing coalition partners further complicate his position. Feijóo blamed the government for two high-speed train collisions that killed 115 people and called Sánchez unfit to lead, while Sánchez warned a PP-Vox coalition would roll back social rights and defended Spain's liberal immigration approach against European trends toward stricter controls.
items.title: Sánchez admits mistakes in Spain's only televised debate before election

items.summary: A Supreme Court bench of justices N Kotiswar Singh and NV Anjaria ruled that an unwed mother has a stronger prima facie claim to custody of her minor child, directing the father—a lawyer running a firm with around 53 associates—to hand over interim custody of their four-year-old son to his German-based mother in Singapore. The court held this preferential position cannot be negated by the absence of marriage or any particular statute, while clarifying it does not exclude the father's claim but establishes only her better prima facie standing; no legal provision disables a young mother from such a claim. On welfare grounds, both parents were found equally capable and free of diagnosable psychiatric disorders, yet the court judged the mother's proposal more beneficial because she had made concrete schooling arrangements in Singapore and could adjust her work schedule, whereas the father would likely depend on relatives and nannies given his demanding practice; it expressed doubt that he could spare adequate time for an energetic four-year-old. A NIMHANS report found the child had been out of formal schooling for about four months with resulting behavioural difficulties and recommended resuming classes promptly, while noting the boy's fluency in German and English reflected a closer bond with his mother; the court rejected the father's argument that relocation would uproot him, observing stability comes from people and routines rather than geography. The decision is confined to interim custody: the mother must obtain a mirror order from a competent Singapore court within three weeks, deposit ₹1 crore, grant daily video access of at least 20 minutes plus visitation in Singapore and custody during visits to India, and bring the child back for school vacations exceeding seven days; the Family Court at Delhi will independently decide permanent guardianship. The article is reporting by Utkarsh Anand of Hindustan Times.
items.title: Supreme Court gives unwed mother a better prima facie claim to custody of her child

items.summary: Delhi Police and Noida STF officials said on Friday that gangster Naseem Durrani was killed during a joint police operation in Bulandshahr. He had been suspected of involvement in the November 16 shooting death of Sameer outside Delhi law minister Kapil Mishra's camp office in Sonia Vihar, northeast Delhi; investigators reported around 16 rounds were fired at the victim. Durrani reportedly has about 25 criminal cases against him and was linked to underworld operative Chhota Shakeel. The claim that he was killed is attributed only to police officials.
items.title: Gangster Naseem Durrani killed in joint police operation in Bulandshahr

items.summary: A car caught fire shortly after ramming a lorry from behind in the early hours of Friday on the Kokapet Outer Ring Road (ORR) near Hyderabad. The vehicle was travelling from Shamshabad toward Kokapet and carried two people at the time, all of whom survived with no casualties reported. Police reached the scene to investigate and registered a case; further details were pending as of report.
items.title: Car catches fire after rear-ending lorry on Kokapet ORR; no casualties reported

items.summary: The foreign ministers of Jordan, the UAE, Indonesia, Pakistan, Türkiye, Algeria, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Kuwait, Libya, Maldives, Egypt and Niger issued a joint statement welcoming the United Kingdom's and Australia's decisions to impose sanctions over Israeli settlement activities in the occupied West Bank. The declaration calls for greater accountability against entities and individuals involved in settlement expansion and annexation policies, including what it terms the E1 settlement plan east of occupied East Jerusalem. It also welcomed the UK sanctioning an organisation accused of obstructing humanitarian aid to Gaza. The ministers described the measures as consistent with international law and UN Security Council Resolution 2334 (2016) and the International Court of Justice's July 19, 2024 advisory opinion, reiterated calls for Israel to rescind settlement-related measures, condemned Israeli military escalation in Gaza, endorsed Trump's Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict, and affirmed support for a two-State solution based on the June 4, 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as capital. The statement is an agency feed not edited by FPJ's editorial team.
items.title: Fifteen Arab and Islamic nations welcome UK and Australia sanctions on Israeli West Bank settlements

items.summary: Indian fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah took four wickets in 29 overs during the first Test versus New Zealand. The article presents several of his statements as reflections on mindset: that concentrating on one ball at a time reduces pressure; that success requires work rather than talent alone, since nothing comes easy; that focusing on process instead of chasing results is key to goals; and that clarity about plans improves execution. These quotes are offered by the source as illustrations of Bumrah's approach, with the article drawing inferences—such as claims that his focus 'helps manage pressure' or makes him 'act with confidence'—that extend beyond what he literally said.
items.title: Jasprit Bumrah quotes on focus and process, framed around a four-wicket Test performance against New Zealand

items.summary: Marathon Petroleum's Martinez Renewables facility northeast of San Francisco was cited by California's Cal/OSHA for 10 violations, three classified as serious: inadequate training, uninsulated high-temperature equipment and faulty emergency eyewash stations. The citations followed a strike that turned into a June lockout after Marathon rejected the union's unconditional return-to-work offer during contract negotiations over fatigue from chronic understaffing and overtime shifts. Workers reported frequent intense flaring with 20-foot flames once they left their April 27 shift, prompting United Steelworkers Local 5 president Nick Plurkowski to call Cal/OSHA the next day; inspectors found at least a dozen employees untrained, including two shift supervisors and 10 operators. The violations echo findings from the U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board's March 2025 report on the November 2022 explosion that killed operator Jerome Serrano during the plant's transition to renewable fuels, which attributed the incident to inadequate operating procedures, burner training and engineering controls. Marathon spokesperson Jamal Kheiry said Martinez Renewables has appealed the citations and disputed them by stating it continues staffing the facility with qualified personnel; a Cal/OSHA spokesperson confirmed the appeal and declined further comment pending resolution. Negotiations are scheduled to resume Dec. 1 with federal mediation support, though Plurkowski doubted good faith after six months of lockout.
items.title: California fined Marathon over safety violations at Martinez Renewables refinery amid worker lockout

items.summary: Police officials say gangster Naseem Durrani was killed during a joint operation by the Delhi Police and Noida Special Task Force (STF) that broke out into an encounter in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh. He had been tracked after police received intelligence about his presence there following the November 16 shooting of Sameer outside the office of Delhi Law Minister Kapil Mishra; armed assailants reportedly fired around 20 rounds at Sameer before he died at a hospital. Durrani is alleged to be linked to Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company and Chhota Shakeel, who reportedly assigned him in 2016 to kill jailed gangster Chhota Rajan, and is also accused of plotting the assassination of journalist Tarek Fatah; he faced more than 25 criminal cases. The killing comes amid an investigation into Sameer's murder, which was suspected to stem from a rivalry between Durrani and Haroon Saifi gangs, though Sameer had reportedly been detained for questioning in another case before being released. Further details on the encounter, exchange of fire, and Durrani's alleged role remain awaited.
items.title: Naseem Durrani killed in Delhi Police-Noida STF encounter in Bulandshahr, UP

items.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron called on Ukraine's allies at a Berlin 'Coalition of the Willing' summit, co-hosted with Germany and the UK, to speed up delivery of air defence systems and "reopen the question" of Ukraine's accession to NATO. He framed this as necessary given what he described as Russia's maximalist position, prioritising deployment of anti-missile systems and interceptors. The summit drew more than 25 leaders alongside President Volodymyr Zelensky, taking place hours after a three-way US-Russia-China summit in Shenzhen where Trump, Putin and Xi reportedly agreed a peace declaration that Macron said does not reorganise the world. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expected new Ukraine peace talks soon on neutral ground, naming the United Arab Emirates as a possible location without giving a date; British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged continued support for Ukraine. US envoy Jared Kushner reported Trump supported European involvement in any deal and was open to extending an Article Five-like security guarantee to Ukraine if it served American interests, while Zelensky said a real guarantee would require US or European forces and bases on Ukrainian territory.
items.title: Macron urges allies to reopen Ukraine's NATO membership question

items.summary: Nobel economist Joseph Stiglitz said recent youth protests across Europe are "legitimate" complaints, attributing them to intergenerational inequality in which young people cannot afford housing or adequate education. Hundreds of thousands protested in France, Denmark, Italy and Spain over rising living costs, a housing crisis and poor pay; the article reports these figures as reported events rather than Stiglitz's own claims. In Spain, protesters held a nationwide 24-hour strike for the first time since 2012 amid reports that some rent €460 a month for a five-square-metre bedroom in Barcelona, though this is presented as an individual account rather than a general statistic. Stiglitz said "part of the problem [...] is inequality across generations" and warned that rising inequality, climate change and AI-related anxieties create uncertainty for younger people who may never match their parents' living standards; these are his characterizations, not established facts about future outcomes. He endorsed taxing the ultra-wealthy as a way to fund public services, citing French economist Gabriel Zucman's proposal of roughly two per cent on fortunes above €100 million and arguing such taxes should be levied at EU level because free movement makes tax avoidance easier; this is Stiglitz advocating a specific proposal rather than it being established policy. He cautioned that taxation alone would not resolve Europe's challenges, recommending public spending reform and more flexible pension systems to reflect longer life expectancy and physically demanding jobs.
items.title: Joseph Stiglitz backs European youth protests as legitimate and calls for taxing the ultra-wealthy

items.summary: A jury at Winchester Crown Court found four British men guilty on Thursday of multiple sexual offences, including rape, against Joanne Young, 49, whose then-husband Philip Young had drugged her and advertised her for sex online. Police uncovered hundreds of intimate images after investigating Mr Young in 2024 over uploading bestiality imagery, exposing a wider pattern of abuse; he filmed her without consent at their Swindon home. The four men, aged between 32 and 62, were convicted after being recruited online: Norman Macksoni (48) was found guilty of rape; Richard Wilkins (62) of rape and assault by penetration; Connor Sanderson-Doyle (32) of assault by penetration and sexual touching; Mohammed Hassan of sexual touching. Mr Young had earlier pleaded guilty to dozens of offences, including 11 counts of rape and 11 counts of administering a substance with intent. A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton (47), admitted one count of assault by penetration, two counts of sexual assault and one count of rape. Justice Pushpinder Saini said the four men faced significant prison sentences and praised Ms Young's bravery. She waived her anonymity, expressed relief at the verdicts, urged other victims to come forward saying they "can be believed and understood," and described how the abuse had cost her life as she knew it. The case was likened by reporting to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France.
items.title: Four British men convicted of raping a woman drugged and advertised by husband

items.summary: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston told Semafor that his proposed $115 billion all-stock merger with chipmaker Marvell has been unpopular, describing it as 'a rough go.' The deal combines Lumentum's optical technology business into Marvell's chips businesses. Shares in both companies fell roughly 40% since the announcement on April 23 over concerns about AI trade runway and claims that Lumentum sold too soon. Hurlston said he expects shares to rebound as more information reaches analysts, while acknowledging a material adverse change clause exists but noting its exercise conditions are limited. He cited an 80% overlap in shareholder bases between the two companies as a source of forced selling among portfolio managers holding one stock but not the other. The merger faces regulatory review in both the US and China, with scrutiny heightened by the Nvidia chip scandal; Hurlston said he and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have previously navigated SAMR approvals. Separately, Semafor reported that Murphy could be considered for Nvidia's CEO role after Jensen Huang's resignation, a possibility Hurlston acknowledged without confirming.
items.title: Lumentum's CEO defends $115 billion all-stock deal with Marvell amid investor backlash

items.summary: ExxonMobil announced that total Guyana oil production topped 1 million barrels per day, a milestone reached seven years after first oil in 2019. The Stabroek Block, developed by Exxon along with partners Hess and CNOOC since the company acquired it in 1999, yielded discoveries estimated at over 11 billion barrels of crude; these figures are reported claims rather than verified totals. Rystad Energy analyst Schreiner Parker told the Financial Times that Guyana was a textbook example of right place, right time and became one of ExxonMobil's crown jewels in its repositioning, with development speed from first oil to over 1 million barrels per day described as seemingly achievable only by ExxonMobil; these are attributed opinions. The article frames this success against the green investment movement that pushed exploration aside after the Paris Agreement, arguing forecasts of near-term peak oil demand have not materialized and that European Union oil and gas imports did not slump during a Middle East supply disruption but moved slightly lower while rising in value because of price shocks; these are claims rather than established facts. The piece asserts that other Big Oil majors are now returning to frontier regions for production boosts instead of divesting assets into solar and battery businesses, citing South America (Suriname, Brazil, Argentina), a Venezuela back on the map after U.S. involvement in its oil industry, Africa, and Asia as destinations; these are reported plans rather than outcomes.
items.title: Guyana's oil boom rekindles frontier drilling among major oil companies

items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to surpass $3 billion in its first week, a figure that would eclipse the lifetime grosses of some major films and concert tours. The Economist argues this windfall coincides with industry mass layoffs, suggesting developers face shrinking incentives to create comparable titles as hardware costs rise and generative AI pushes smaller teams toward lower-spec games; these are presented as arguments rather than established outcomes. The New York Times Magazine reviewed the game favorably, praising it as a satisfying simulacrum of American life amid claims that the United States resembles one of its settings.
items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI projected to exceed $3 billion in first-week sales

items.summary: An expert on U.S.-China relations at Harvard Kennedy School assessed the Nov. 19, 2026 trilateral meeting of Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, held during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, arguing it delivered more style than substance. The author attributes this to heavy symbolism: Xi greeting Trump at the airport (a special honor) and an unprecedented hug between them were choreographed displays; seating Xi centrally framed China as a steadying 'Middle Kingdom,' which the writer notes reflects how Xi wants Beijing seen rather than its actual global presence. On policy, all three agreed reforming the U.N. is needed with China seeking more power while Trump grows disillusioned, and they signed a document on nuclear controls built around Reagan-Gorbachev's 1985 phrase 'Nuclear war cannot be won, must never be fought,' though it contained few commitments given expired treaties and Beijing lagging in capacity; the author flags that Beijing may hold different views. The writer asserts the wars in Iran (ongoing roughly nine months) and Ukraine were not discussed substantively—Ukraine by name at all—with speculation that China or Russia could have helped pressure Iran but neither was willing to offer assistance, while Europe's absence made a Trump-Ukraine statement impractical; AI regulation and critical mineral supply chains are said not to have been raised publicly though possibly in bilateral talks. Comparing it to the 1945 Yalta Conference, the author notes differences: Britain was part of that 'big three' but China is absent now, and Stalin-Roosevelt-Churchill were comrades-in-arms who later drifted apart as the Cold War began, whereas here China and Russia are partners with the U.S. seen as their adversary; the writer speculates Trump may want détente rather than a new Cold War and questions whether Europe will object to such an emerging order.
items.title: Harvard Kennedy School expert characterizes Xi-Putin-Trump Shenzhen summit as symbolic with little policy substance

items.summary: Olivia Cheung, welcomed by Genie Godula, describes the Xi Jinping-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting at the APEC summit as significant despite lacking concrete agreements. She attributes its importance to what she calls "the precedence of the United States seeing and giving recognition that China and Russia are peers of the United States," arguing that this framing produces a notable image of a G3, though these assessments remain Cheung's interpretation rather than established outcomes or commitments from the meeting itself.
items.title: Olivia Cheung characterizes Trump's framing of China and Russia as US 'peers' at a trilateral APEC meeting.

items.summary: The Dutch data protection authority, Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP), advised people not to buy AI-enabled smart glasses available on the Dutch market, following tests of six unnamed devices that ranged in price from under €100 (£84) to over €500 and came from different continents. The AP reported that during testing one pair repeatedly told a user an ambulance was en route when emergency services had not actually been contacted; another gave dating advice to an adult who expressed romantic interest in a minor, while others misread medicine packaging instructions and severe weather warnings. Beyond AI reliability, the authority flagged privacy risks including secret filming with obscured recording lights that some manufacturers claimed would disable the device but still functioned, security flaws allowing nearby users to connect without permission or operate cameras remotely, and data often exported outside the EU. The AP stopped short of calling for a ban on sale; it said its investigation focused mainly on algorithms and AI rather than data protection, though broader concerns about non-consensual filming remain. Meta recently released glasses without a camera amid privacy backlash, but whether they were tested is unknown, as was whether any of the three manufacturers approached by the BBC (Meta, TCL, HTC) had products in the test set.
items.title: Dutch privacy watchdog advises against buying AI smart glasses after testing six models

items.summary: Swedish advanced nuclear developer Blykalla signed an agreement on Nov. 12, announced Nov. 16, that the companies describe as the world's first high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) enrichment contract for a commercial lead-cooled reactor. The deal covers Blykalla's first commercial SEALER unit, its 55-MWe Swedish Advanced Lead Reactor planned for U.S. deployment; under it, Blykalla supplies the uranium feed and Urenco enriches material at its Capenhurst facility in England, which is expected online by 2031 with deliveries to begin in the early 2030s. Neither company disclosed the contract value or enrichment level for SEALER fuel; Stedman said only that it secures HALEU enrichment for "at least our first commercial unit." The agreement covers just the enrichment stage, not finished-fuel supply, which Blykalla has not identified and is developing through an integrated sourcing strategy. This is Urenco's third HALEU contract after Radiant (Sept. 2025) and Antares Nuclear (May 2026). The DOE defines HALEU as uranium enriched above 5% but below 20%, versus up to 5% for typical commercial reactor fuel, and has projected domestic demand could reach 50 metric tons annually by 2035. Urenco received £196 million in May 2024 under a program committing up to £300 million; the Capenhurst facility totals roughly £400 million with an initial capacity of up to 27 metric tons of HALEU annually, designed for future expansion.
items.title: Blykalla signs world's first HALEU enrichment contract for a commercial lead-cooled reactor with Urenco.

items.summary: Experts attribute rising human-wildlife conflict in Sri Lanka to habitat fragmentation from deforestation, food-search behavior by displaced species, improved road connectivity via expressways, and a decline in predators. Peacocks have spread from the dry zone into Colombo's wet-zone suburbs since 2020; Sarath Kotagama links this partly to people altering vegetation and temperature conditions enabling movement across cleared strips such as those beside the Southern Expressway (about 300 meters of open habitat). Primatologist Charmalie Nahallage says purple-faced leaf langurs, forced onto rooftops by fragmented forest, become pests when fed or given access to dumped food waste. Ceylon spotted deer in Homagama number roughly 1,500-2,500 and are increasingly hit on roads; the Department of Wildlife Conservation has successfully translocated recovered animals to Udawalawe National Park (about 118 kilometers southeast of Colombo). At Attidiya center, wildlife veterinarian Pramuditha Devasurendra reported that in 2025 there were 4,855 cases total: 1,822 mammals, 1,879 birds and 1,154 reptiles and other species; recoveries totaled 643 mammals, 675 birds and 848 reptiles (2,167 animals released). He said about 80% of cases involve electrocution or road accidents, air rifle attacks on monkeys have risen since 2018, and recovery rates are roughly 70% for serpents/reptiles versus 20-25% for monkeys. Hasini Sarathchandra (DWC) noted peacock numbers may spike because jackals that ate their eggs have declined; Nahallage added that urban rattlesnakes feeding on the same prey are now rarely seen, illustrating disrupted food webs. Kotagama argues coexistence requires people to accept these animals as non-pests rather than targets of air rifles and electrocution.
items.title: Sri Lankan wild animals increasingly move into cities as habitat is fragmented and predators decline

items.summary: The European Union, via a statement from the European Commission's diplomatic service on 20 November 2026, urged Myanmar to fully and immediately comply with an International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruling. The bloc framed compliance as mandatory under international law rather than optional, calling for restitution and compensation where damage is not remedied through restitution, and stated that accountability for crimes against the Rohingya was essential to a sustainable resolution of the crisis and regional stability. EU officials described the ICJ's independence and authority as more important amid threats to peace and widespread violations of international law, urging all states to respect its decisions. The statement followed the UN court's Thursday ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017 during military operations in northern Rakhine State, a decision reached by a vote of 9-6 and marking the first time the ICJ held a state responsible for genocide.
items.title: EU urges Myanmar to implement ICJ genocide ruling without delay

items.summary: Analysts note that crude oil exports from the Persian Gulf have rebounded near pre-war levels, while Brent slid to about $92 per barrel from a late-October peak above $118. The market and most analysts assume steady Middle Eastern flows will continue into next year and eventually produce an oil surplus; investment banks and the IEA expect that surplus as early as this quarter, with Goldman Sachs projecting Brent averaging $88 in 2027 under its base case of no diplomatic breakthrough. However, inbound tanker traffic to Hormuz is at risk: since late August, empty-tanker capacity bound for the Gulf of Oman fell roughly 40%, and combined ballasting supertanker and Suezmax capacity there dropped from 130 million barrels on Aug. 31 to 71 million as of Nov. 16, per Tankertrackers.com cited by Bloomberg; co-founder Samir Madani said "not enough vacant tankers" exist to take oil out of the region. Meanwhile tanker attacks intensified—five vessels were struck near Hormuz between Nov. 11 and 18, per Windward—and IEA and Goldman both flag that shipping-attack risks undermine their surplus forecasts.
items.title: Tanker Shortage Threatens Hormuz Oil Exports Despite Recovery
